A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same task-language and manipulator research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original Spriteworld and face-editing experiments, MNIST classifier comparisons, and sentiment-manipulation results, with experimental details in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices C–D, and adds a learned-stack demonstration in Section 2.4.

M1.justification: v2 adds an auxiliary differentiable stack with learned push/pop operations and Empty/PshPop objectives (Task 2.12). The core manipulator specification, strong and complement variants, and linear specialization remain; expanded explanations do not establish changes to their implementations.

E1.justification: The stack adds a storage-and-retrieval task on existing Spriteworld data. The principal image and sentiment datasets remain, including IMDB failure observations. However, v1's separately reported MNIST classifier-bootstrapping scenarios, including active learning, are absent from v2.

E2.justification: v1 Section 3.3's separate comparison between manipulator-assisted gets and plain classifiers disappears. The retained MNIST copying comparison still uses direct classifier copying and VAEs, and Table 1 retains all B-GST conditions and the human reference. CycleGAN remains a theoretical comparison.

E3.justification: The new stack experiment introduces a protocol using 16-dimensional image latents, a 64-dimensional stack, a 256-unit MLP, and 100,000 training steps with batch size 64. The retained manipulation, VAE and sentiment experiments preserve their documented settings despite relocation.

E4.justification: v2 removes the analysis testing whether synthetic outputs and differing get/put inductive biases improve MNIST classification under supervised, unsupervised and active learning. Existing derived-attribute, latent-space and successive-classifier analyses remain. Appendix B's new conceptual failure examples are not additional empirical robustness tests.

E5.justification: The new stack methodology explicitly supplies seed 0. Existing image-experiment seeds remain unchanged, and the MNIST comparison still reports 20 repetitions with one-standard-deviation shading. There is no reported increase in repetitions or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds qualitative recovery of four shapes using the learned stack. The separate classifier-bootstrapping null finding is removed. Existing sentiment Table 1 values, image-editing examples and MNIST degradation curves are retained; v1 Figure 5(b) becomes v2 Figure 8.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds substantial PROP/operad constructions formalizing universal approximators and specialization. The Bayesian-inversion derivation replaces the entropy-balancer formulation with explicit latent-split inverse conditions. Definition 3.9 also changes optimal partial solutions from requiring all divergence/combiner choices to a given choice. These exceed relocation of the earlier proofs.

C1.justification: The central task-language and manipulator contributions remain. v2 adds the claim that manipulation is the first natural problem class for multi-learner multi-objective learning (Section 1.1), and claims maximal permissible generality among comparable editing tasks (Section 5.2). These extend its novelty claims without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations and boundaries: Appendix B.4 links instability to parameter dependencies, Appendix D.2 explains identity collapse through competing task losses and qualifies direct generative-classifier interpretation, and Section 5.3 identifies limitations of equational characterization and unresolved analysis of dynamic/adversarial tasks. These go beyond v1's broader scale and domain cautions.

D1.justification: The stack methodology adds concrete architecture, preprocessing, GPU-use, optimization and training-budget details. Existing Spriteworld, face, MNIST, VAE and sentiment implementation information is largely preserved across Appendices C–D; moving those details does not establish changed experiments.

R1.justification: New Section 5.2 substantively positions the framework against categorical deep learning, generalized variational inference and mainstream neurosymbolic approaches, with added references. Appendix A.2 also explicitly connects and attributes specialization semantics to On the Anatomy of Attention, previously cited mainly as a future connection.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion are extensively rewritten, with worked introductory examples and an explicit contributions section. Mathematical preliminaries move to Appendix A, manipulation proofs move into Section 3, experiments are separated into Section 4 and Appendix D, and the conclusion gains dedicated positioning and limitations subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adds the stack illustration and numerous explanatory/formal diagrams, revises diagram notation, and substantially reformats the document. v1's combined MNIST Figure 5 is split into v2 Figures 3 and 8, while Table 1 moves to Appendix D. Existing figures are resized and redistributed.

improvement.justification: The worked examples, stack demonstration, expanded specialization formalism and explicit limitations make the framework more accessible and better contextualized. The gain is limited by unchanged benchmark evidence, omission of the classifier-bootstrapping null result, and new mathematical inconsistencies: the combined manipulation loss on page 9 targets a rather than d in GetPut and omits Undoability's comparison argument, contradicting the atomic formulas above it.
